motions.item_title: Approve the minutes of October 28, 2025, Planning Commission meeting. Commissioner Strong secon…
motions.motion: Commissioner Whiting moved to approve the minutes of October 28, 2025, Planning Commission meeting. Commissioner Strong seconded the motion.
motions.headline: October 28 minutes approved
motions.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its October 28, 2025 meeting.
motions.impact: This makes the commission's record of that meeting official. You will not notice it.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.A., General Plan Amendment – Moderate Income H…
motions.motion: Commissioner Whiting moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.A., General Plan Amendment – Moderate Income Housing. Commissioner Hess seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Moderate income housing section of the general plan
motions.summary: The commission recommended the council amend the moderate income housing section of the city's general plan, the long-range document that guides growth.
motions.impact: The motion does not say what the amendment changes. It takes effect only if the council approves it, and it changes no rule on your property by itself.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.B., Alternative Animal Management Plans and Ot…
motions.motion: Commissioner Whiting moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.B., Alternative Animal Management Plans and Other Zoning Provisions, with the change that the Planning Commission is the revocation authority instead of the planning director or the code enforcement officer. Commissioner Free seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Revocable permits for alternative animal plans
motions.summary: The commission recommended the council adopt rules on alternative animal management plans and other zoning provisions, with the commission, not staff, able to revoke a plan.
motions.impact: If you keep animals under an alternative plan, the commission would decide whether you lose it, not the planning director or code enforcement officer. Nothing changes until the council votes.
